questions.question: Which intended visitor's problem should Version B lead with?
questions.why_ambiguous: The product can help individual maintainers and teams, but source capabilities alone do not establish which is the intended lead market.
questions.consequence: Changes the protagonist, opening situation, value framing, storyboard, and page hierarchy.

options.label: Individual builder maintaining a long project
options.tradeoff: Concrete emotional burden; may underrepresent team coordination

options.label: Team lead coordinating shared project work
options.tradeoff: Broader governance needs; can drift into audit language

options.label: Neither; I will correct the lead user and problem

questions.question: Which main promise is acceptable without claiming measured time savings?
questions.why_ambiguous: Source verifies specified mechanisms more readily than externally observed adoption outcomes or quantitative improvements.
questions.consequence: Controls hero promise, marketing proof, image text, and what QA must verify.

options.label: Position as returning attention to the real project work
options.tradeoff: Qualitative intended benefit, not a guaranteed result

options.label: Lead with durable project context across sessions
options.tradeoff: Risks narrowing the integrated system into only PCM

options.label: Neither; propose different benefit and limits

questions.question: What should the Version B demo CTA actually be permitted to do?
questions.why_ambiguous: A preview, simulation, local installer, and live-repository action have different user expectations and side-effect risks.
questions.consequence: Changes UX flow, CTA wording, service blueprint and any permissible network/file operations.

options.label: Read-only illustration or preview, with clear disclosure
Direct link to actual pinned setup instructions; no browser write
